answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying every identity to a bonded work ledger: to join, an agent deposits a small stake and completes a chain of real tasks for distinct peers, each completion sealed with a cipher signature and recorded on a public ledge. New identities start with zero trust and gain spending rights only as verified work history grows, so one operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand stakes and perform a thousand distinct jobs. Like copper wiring, the cost scales with every added node: cheap for one honest agent, ruinous at Sybil scale.
